I need a reliable way to detect when the baseline is done. The baseline script prints a line containing “final results” when it finishes, so I can poll the log file for that string. A simple `until grep -q "final results" /tmp/r0_baseline.log` loop will suffice, sleeping a short interval (30 seconds) between checks to avoid hammering the filesystem.

Once the baseline is confirmed finished, I should give it a brief grace period (maybe 15 seconds) to ensure any final I/O settles, then extract the run directory path that the baseline printed. Looking at the baseline log, there’s a line like “run directory …” that contains the directory path as the last field. I can pull that out with `grep "run directory" /tmp/r0_baseline.log | head -1 | awk '{print $NF}'`. I’ll store that in a variable `R0_DIR` for later use.

Now I need to launch each of the five experiments in order, capturing their stdout/stderr to separate log files under `/tmp`. The experiments are invoked via the `exp.py` script, using the appropriate experiment name and a numeric argument (the “2” seems to be the default seed or something). For the “proc_after” and “oec_after” experiments, they require the path to the champion checkpoint from the baseline and the baseline run directory itself. Those can be constructed as `$R0_DIR/merges/champion.pt` and `$R0_DIR`.

I’ll run each experiment with the virtual environment’s Python interpreter: `.venv/bin/python exp.py <experiment> 2`. I’ll redirect both stdout and stderr to `/tmp/rX_<experiment>.log` and then echo the exit status (`$?`) immediately after each run so I can see if any of them fail.

Finally, after all five have been attempted, I’ll print “ALL EXPERIMENTS DONE” to mark completion.

To keep everything tidy and reproducible, I’ll write this whole sequence into a temporary shell script (`/tmp/run_experiments.sh`). I’ll use a heredoc (`cat > /tmp/run_experiments.sh << 'EOF' ... EOF`) to embed the script content, then `chmod +x` to make it executable. After creating the script, I’ll execute it immediately. Since the script itself contains a blocking `until` loop, it will naturally wait for the baseline to finish before proceeding, so I can run it in the background to avoid tying up the current session. I’ll add `run_in_background: true` to the tool call so the system knows not to wait for its completion.

All of this matches the desired behavior: queue all five paper experiments after the baseline finishes, with proper logging and exit-code reporting. The exact bash commands, variable names, and file paths need to be precise to avoid any syntax errors.

cat > /tmp/run_experiments.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
cd /home/lane/MythosMini
until grep -q "final results" /tmp/r0_baseline.log 2>/dev/null; do sleep 30; done
sleep 15
R0_DIR=$(grep "run directory" /tmp/r0_baseline.log | head -1 | awk '{print $NF}')
echo "baseline done: $R0_DIR"
.venv/bin/python exp.py deepthin 2 > /tmp/r1_deepthin.log 2>&1
echo "deepthin exit: $?"
.venv/bin/python exp.py proc 2 > /tmp/r2_proc.log 2>&1
echo "proc exit: $?"
.venv/bin/python exp.py oec 2 > /tmp/r3_oec.log 2>&1
echo "oec exit: $?"
.venv/bin/python exp.py proc_after "$R0_DIR/merges/champion.pt" "$R0_DIR" > /tmp/r4_proc_after.log 2>&1
echo "proc_after exit: $?"
.venv/bin/python exp.py oec_after "$R0_DIR/merges/champion.pt" "$R0_DIR" > /tmp/r5_oec_after.log 2>&1
echo "oec_after exit: $?"
echo "ALL EXPERIMENTS DONE"
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/run_experiments.sh
/tmp/run_experiments.sh; echo "queue exit: $?"
